about: Story Time. level: 0 = LKG, -1 = UKG, 1-5 = Class. {name} = the child's name. Actor = [emoji, x%, y% (feet), size % of width, animation (bob hop fly walk shake grow spin float flip gold)]. Quiz answer 'a' must be one of the options 'o'.

pages.text: Hop, hop! This is Bunny.
Bunny is hungry.
Bunny finds one, two, three carrots!
Here comes Duck. Duck is hungry too.
Bunny shares a carrot with Duck. Yum! Friends share.

quiz.q: Who is this story about?
What did Bunny find?
Who did Bunny share with?

pages.text: {name} has a big red balloon.
Whoosh! The wind blows.
The balloon flies up, up, up!
A kind bird brings it back.
Thank you, bird! {name} is happy.

quiz.q: What colour is the balloon?
What blew the balloon away?
Who brought the balloon back?

pages.text: It was a hot day. The crow was thirsty.
The crow saw a pot with a little water.
Its beak could not reach. Oh no!
The crow had an idea! It dropped in pebbles.
Plop, plop! The water came up.
The crow drank and flew away happy!

quiz.q: What did the crow want?
What did the crow drop into the pot?
How did the crow feel at the end?

pages.text: A little ant went to drink water.
Splash! The ant fell in. Help!
A dove dropped a leaf for the ant.
The ant climbed on the leaf. Safe!
A hunter wanted to catch the dove.
The ant bit his foot. The dove flew away!
Friends help each other.

quiz.q: Who fell into the water?
What did the dove drop to help?
Who saved the dove?

pages.text: A big lion was sleeping under a tree.
A mouse woke him up. The lion caught her!
"Let me go, and I will help you one day." The lion let her go.
Later, the lion was caught in a hunter's net.
The mouse came and cut the net with her teeth.
The lion was free! "Thank you, little friend!"
Even a small friend can be a big help.

quiz.q: Where was the lion sleeping?
What caught the lion?
How did the mouse help the lion?

pages.text: Grandma gave {name} a tiny seed.
{name} planted it and gave it water.
Every day, the sun gave it light.
One morning, a green shoot popped out!
The plant grew taller. New leaves came out.
A flower opened! A bee came to say hello.
Plants need soil, water, air and sunlight.

quiz.q: What did Grandma give?
What came out of the soil first?
What do plants need to grow?

pages.text: Hare was fast. "Nobody can beat me!" he said.
Tortoise said, "Let us have a race." Everyone laughed.
The race began! Hare ran far ahead.
"Tortoise is so slow. I will take a nap."
Tortoise kept walking, slow and steady.
Hare woke up. But Tortoise had already won!
Slow and steady wins the race.

quiz.q: Who was faster?
Why did Hare lose the race?
What is the lesson of the story?
quiz.a: Slow and steady wins the race
o: Slow and steady wins the race
Never take part in a race

pages.text: A monkey lived on a jamun tree by the river.
He gave jamuns to a crocodile. They became friends.
The crocodile's wife said, "Bring me the monkey's heart!"
The crocodile said, "Come home with me." The monkey sat on his back.
In the river, he said, "My wife wants your heart!"
The monkey said, "I left my heart on the tree. Take me back!"
Back on land, the monkey climbed the tree. "Goodbye!"
Stay calm and think fast when you are in trouble.

quiz.q: Which fruit did the monkey eat?
What did the crocodile's wife want?
How did the monkey save himself?

stories.title: The Goose with the Golden Eggs

pages.text: A poor farmer had a goose. One morning, something shone in its nest.
It was an egg of pure gold! The farmer sold it for food.
Every day the goose laid one golden egg. The farmer became rich.
But he became greedy. "I want all the eggs at once!"
He chased the goose and squeezed it hard.
The frightened goose flew far away and never came back.
Now he had no goose and no eggs. He was sorry.
Greed can make us lose what we already have.

quiz.q: What was special about the goose?
Why did the farmer lose the goose?
What does 'greedy' mean?

pages.text: {name} went to the park. There was rubbish everywhere!
A robot rolled up. "Hi {name}, I am Robo! Let's clean up."
"Green bin for wet waste like peels. Blue bin for paper and plastic."
{name} put peels in the green bin and bottles in the blue bin.
"Wet waste becomes compost. Plastic and paper get recycled!"
Soon the park was clean. The birds came back.
Reduce, reuse and recycle. Keep our Earth clean!

quiz.q: Which bin should banana peels go in?
What can wet waste become?
What does 'recycle' mean?
quiz.a: Making new things from old things
o: Making new things from old things

pages.text: Akbar said, "Stand in the icy lake all night and win a reward!"
A poor man stood in the freezing water all night.
He said, "I looked at a far-away palace lamp."
"The lamp kept you warm. No reward!" said Akbar.
Akbar found Birbal cooking khichdi, the pot hanging high above a tiny fire.
"It will never cook!" laughed Akbar. "Nor can a far lamp warm a man," said Birbal.
Akbar understood and gave the man his reward.

quiz.q: Where did the poor man stand all night?
Why could Birbal's khichdi not cook?
quiz.a: The fire was too far away
o: The fire was too far away

quiz.q: What did Birbal want Akbar to understand?
quiz.a: A far-away lamp cannot give warmth
o: A far-away lamp cannot give warmth

pages.text: {name} put on a space suit. 3, 2, 1... Blast off!
The rocket zoomed up into space.
Earth looked like a blue ball. {name} floated! The suit gives air to breathe.
The rocket landed on the Moon. It had big holes called craters.
{name} jumped very high! The Moon's gravity is weaker.
The sky was black, because the Moon has no air.
{name} planted a flag, waved at Earth, and flew home.

quiz.q: What are the big holes on the Moon called?
Why could {name} jump so high on the Moon?
Why is the Moon's sky black in the daytime?

pages.text: There was little rain. Tenali Raman's garden was dry.
One night, Tenali saw thieves hiding near his house.
He said loudly, "Let us hide our gold in the well!"
He dropped a box of stones into the well. Splash!
All night, the thieves pulled up buckets of water. It flowed into the garden.
By morning the garden was watered. The box had only stones!
"Thank you for watering my garden!" laughed Tenali. Brains beat muscles.

quiz.q: Why was Tenali's garden dry?
What was really inside the box?
Who watered Tenali's garden?

pages.text: The puddle outside school was gone! "Where did the water go?" asked {name}.
The Sun's heat turned water into vapour. This is evaporation.
The vapour cooled into tiny drops and made clouds. This is condensation.
The drops grew heavy and fell as rain. This is precipitation.
Rain filled rivers, lakes and seas. This is collection.
Then it all started again! {name} found the water cycle.
Case closed! Evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection.

quiz.q: What is evaporation?
Clouds form during…
Which order is right?

pages.text: The moon is up. Hello, Little Owl!
Little Owl says goodnight to the stars.
Goodnight, Cat. Goodnight, Dog.
Little Owl yawns. Time to sleep.
Goodnight, {name}. Sweet dreams!

quiz.q: Who is the story about?
What is in the sky at night?
What does Little Owl do at the end?

pages.text: Five little ducks go for a swim.
Quack, quack! Splash, splash!
Mother Duck calls, "Come home!"
One, two, three, four, five!
All the ducks are home. Hooray!

quiz.q: Who went for a swim?
How many ducks?
Where did the ducks swim?

pages.text: A hungry fox saw some grapes.
The grapes were high up on a vine.
The fox jumped. He could not reach!
He jumped again and again. No luck!
"Those grapes are sour anyway," said the fox.
Don't say bad things about what you cannot get.

quiz.q: What did the fox want?
Who is the story about?
How did the fox feel?

pages.text: {name} played in the garden.
Oh! {name}'s hands are dirty.
Germs are too tiny to see!
{name} washes with soap and water.
Rub, rub, rub! Bubbles everywhere!
Clean hands! Now {name} can eat.

quiz.q: What do we wash hands with?
Where were the hands dirty?
What do we do before we eat?

pages.text: A big elephant wanted to make friends.
"You are too big to play with us," said the monkey.
"You are too big for my home," said the rabbit.
Then a tiger came! All the animals ran away.
The elephant stood tall and trumpeted. The tiger ran off!
"Thank you!" said everyone. "Please be our friend."
Being kind matters more than being big or small.

quiz.q: Who wanted friends?
Who scared the animals?
How did the elephant help?

pages.text: At bedtime, {name} looked out of the window.
The sky was full of twinkling stars!
"One, two, three..." There were too many to count!
Dad said, "Stars are giant suns, very far away."
"Some stars make pictures called constellations."
{name} yawned. "Goodnight, stars!"

quiz.q: When did {name} look at the sky?
What are stars?
Star pictures are called…

pages.text: A shepherd boy looked after sheep near a village.
He was bored. He shouted, "Wolf! Wolf!" as a joke.
The villagers ran to help. There was no wolf! He laughed.
He played the same trick again. The villagers were angry.
Then a real wolf came! "Wolf! Help!" he cried.
Nobody came this time. They thought it was a joke.
If you tell lies, people won't believe you, even when you tell the truth.

quiz.q: What did the boy look after?
Why didn't the villagers come at the end?
What is the lesson?

stories.title: The Clever Rabbit and the Lion

pages.text: A greedy lion ate one animal every day.
One day it was a little rabbit's turn.
The rabbit came late. "Why are you late?" roared the lion.
"Another lion stopped me. He says he is king!"
"Show me!" said the lion. The rabbit took him to a deep well.
The lion saw his reflection and jumped in to fight it. Splash!
The animals were safe. Brains can beat strength!

quiz.q: Whose turn was it?
Where did the rabbit take the lion?
What did the lion see in the water?

pages.text: A hungry jackal went into a village looking for food.
Dogs chased him! He jumped into a tub of blue dye.
He came out bright blue! The forest animals were scared.
"I am your new king, sent from the sky!" he said.
The animals obeyed him. He became proud and lazy.
One night, the jackals howled. He howled too! "Aoooo!"
Now everyone knew he was just a jackal! He ran away. Always be yourself.

quiz.q: What colour did the jackal become?
What did he say he was?
How did the animals find out the truth?

pages.text: {name} found a magnet in the science box.
It pulled pins and paper clips. Click!
But it did not pull a pencil or an eraser.
Magnets pull things made of iron and steel.
A compass has a tiny magnet. It always points north!
{name} solved the mystery: magnets love iron!

quiz.q: What does a magnet pull?
Which one will a magnet NOT pull?
Which tool has a tiny magnet?

pages.text: Akbar asked, "Birbal, how many crows live in our city?"
Everyone laughed. Nobody can count all the crows!
Birbal thought for a moment and said, "95,463 crows!"
"What if there are more?" asked Akbar.
"Then some crows are visiting their relatives!"
"And if there are fewer, some went to visit theirs!" Akbar laughed.

quiz.q: What did Akbar ask Birbal to count?
What did Birbal say if there were more crows?
Why is this story funny?
quiz.a: Birbal gave a clever answer to an impossible question
o: Birbal gave a clever answer to an impossible question

pages.text: A poor woodcutter was cutting wood by a river.
Splash! His axe fell into the deep river.
He cried. A river spirit came up holding a golden axe.
"Is this yours?" "No," said the woodcutter. Then she showed a silver axe. "No."
Then she held up his old iron axe. "Yes! That is mine!"
She gave him all three axes for being honest.
Honesty is the best policy.

quiz.q: What fell into the river?
Why did he say no to the golden axe?
What did he get at the end?

pages.text: King Krishnadevaraya gave each poet a cat and a cow, to keep mice away.
The cats would drink the cows' milk. Everyone's cat grew fat.
Tenali gave his cat a bowl of very hot milk. Ouch! It burnt her nose.
After that, his cat ran away whenever she saw milk!
The king called, "Show me your cats!" Tenali's cat was thin.
"She does not drink milk," said Tenali. The king put milk before her. She ran!
Tenali showed that he had drunk all the milk himself. Everyone laughed, even the king!

quiz.q: What did the king give each poet?
Why did Tenali's cat run from milk?
Who really drank the milk?

pages.text: {name} boarded a spaceship for a tour of the Solar System!
First stop: Mercury, the closest planet to the Sun. Hot!
Next, Venus: the hottest planet, covered in thick clouds.
Then Earth, our home. The only planet we know with life.
Mars is red and dusty. Jupiter is the biggest planet of all!
Saturn has beautiful rings. Uranus and Neptune are icy blue.
Eight planets go around the Sun. What a trip, {name}!

quiz.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
Which is the biggest planet?
How many planets go around the Sun?
